assessment: In this manuscript, the authors introduce a new piece of software, BehaviorDEPOT, that aims to serve as an open-source classifier in service of standard lab-based behavioral assays. The key arguments the authors make are that (1) the open-source code allows for freely available access, (2) the code doesn't require any coding knowledge to build new classifiers, (3) it is generalizable to other behaviors than freezing and other species (although this latter point is not shown), (4) that it uses posture-based tracking that allows for higher resolution than centroid-based methods, and (5) that it is possible to isolate features used in the classifiers. These aims are laudable, the software is indeed relatively easy to use, and it will likely be used widely in the community.
